items.title: Add automatic telemetry reporting for unhandled server errors

findings: QuestarrNG already implements this feature with per-user opt-in telemetry disabled by default, a per-incident consent dialog otherwise, scrubbed logs and error text, one automatic worker submission per detected error, a 30-minute cooldown, owner-bound pending reports with a 24-hour TTL, UUID validation, retryable idempotent sends, and bounded fatal handling for unhandled errors. The dialog distinguishes a real 404 expiry from transient request failures. Upstream review follow-ups are present; its Apprise decoupling proposal was withdrawn because other event notifications use the same in-app preference rule. The fork's per-user socket rooms also prevent notification/report-link leakage across users.
acceptance: Automatic telemetry sends only after the user's explicit setting is enabled; otherwise the user must confirm each report. Diagnostic content is scrubbed before upload, pending reports are owner-scoped and expire, concurrent sends cannot duplicate delivery, and other users cannot receive the notification. The settings screen and consent/retry dialog work as described.

items.title: subdir-app-url image - api/igdb/search does not include base path

findings: The report says IGDB search from Add Game used a raw client fetch, which skipped the subdirectory prefix. QuestarrNG's Add Game flow uses `apiFetch`, which applies the runtime-resolved base path. A focused client test asserts `/Questarr/api/igdb/search`, and the server route test confirms the endpoint succeeds only under the configured prefix.
acceptance: Under a configured `QUESTARR_BASE_PATH`, Add Game sends IGDB search requests to the prefixed endpoint and the server serves that route.

items.title: Fix qBittorrent v5.2+ torrent-file upload success not recognized

findings: The qBittorrent 5.2+ torrent-file upload path handles the JSON success response as a successful add and treats a JSON error response as a failed add. Regression tests cover both outcomes, preventing successful uploads from being reported as errors.
acceptance: When qBittorrent returns JSON after torrent-file upload, success is recognized and a returned API error remains visible as a failure.

items.title: Add opt-in debug logging of full downloader responses

findings: Downloader response diagnostics are opt-in and disabled by default. The implementation bounds response-body reads and redacts sensitive URLs, query values, headers and body content before logging; it covers unsuccessful and authentication responses before their bodies are consumed. The API contract is validated at runtime and the Logs UI handles loading and errors.
acceptance: With diagnostics disabled, downloader responses are not logged. When explicitly enabled, diagnostic output is bounded and scrubbed, including failed and authentication responses, without breaking response handling.

items.title: Raise the Logs page history limit from 200 to 1000 lines

findings: The logs API returns 1,000 lines by default and clamps requests at 5,000; the Logs page requests 1,000 and the server-side rolling buffer retains up to 5,000. The smaller mobile display cap remains in place.
acceptance: The logs endpoint defaults to 1,000 entries, respects its documented bounds up to 5,000, and the Logs page requests the increased history without removing the mobile cap.

items.title: Address review feedback on #927 (downloader debug logging)

findings: This follow-up addresses review feedback on PR #927. The current implementation retains the default-off setting, bounded diagnostic reads and sensitive-value scrubbing across the downloader response logging path; the fixes are exercised by the shared downloader logging regressions.
acceptance: The review follow-up's privacy and response-handling fixes remain present and pass the focused downloader diagnostic tests.

items.title: Fix TS2554 typecheck failure in SendErrorReportDialog

findings: SendErrorReportDialog now passes the issue number expected by buildGitHubIssueUrl, resolving the TS2554 type-check failure. The dialog regression suite passes and repository TypeScript checking succeeds.
acceptance: The issue URL builder receives the required issue number and the client type-checks.

items.title: Fix import modeUsed reporting only the last per-file fallback

findings: PCImportStrategy reports the transfer mode selected for the batch instead of allowing a last-file hardlink fallback to overwrite the batch result. Per-file fallback remains visible separately, with regression coverage for the original mode and file identity.
acceptance: A mixed-result import retains the original batch transfer mode while reporting per-file fallback accurately.

items.title: Port 3 import/download bug fixes from Adarack fork

findings: The three import/download fixes are present with QuestarrNG's multi-user safeguards: imports that need a game link enter a dedicated owner-scoped state and can be relinked through an atomic conditional update; manual NZBGet and SABnzbd imports detect duplicated mapped source paths and report missing sources; completed NZBGet items can resolve DestDir from download history.
acceptance: A pending import can be safely linked to an owned game, stale relink or skip updates cannot overwrite concurrent changes, duplicate or missing manual-import paths produce actionable outcomes, and NZBGet completed-history lookup can recover DestDir.

items.title: Add optional Windows installer build to the deploy pipeline

findings: QuestarrNG contains an opt-in Windows installer workflow and a .NET 10 Windows service wrapper adapted to the fork's deployment model. The self-contained win-x64 service project builds with zero warnings and errors. The Inno Setup script itself has not been compiled: isolated Wine initialization hung and was terminated with its task-owned temporary prefix removed. The latest fork deploy-workflow run inspected skipped the optional installer job, and dispatching the combined workflow for this check would also run the Docker deployment path.
acceptance: Compile the Inno Setup installer with the pinned compiler and confirm the workflow produces the Windows installer artifact and checksum; validate installation and service lifecycle on Windows before marking verified.

items.title: Ignore subagent worktree directories

findings: This repository-hygiene change ignores Claude-created worktree directories. QuestarrNG already ignores .claude/worktrees/ in its root .gitignore, so transient worktree contents do not appear as untracked project files.
acceptance: The root ignore rule covers .claude/worktrees/.

items.title: Ship-now fixes from the Jessomadic/questarr fork review

findings: The PR bundles eight changes. QuestarrNG has a default-deny API authentication boundary with an explicit public-route allowlist; xREL search is bounded to 24 seconds and carries nuke reasons through to the release UI; Newznab and Torznab capability discovery tries candidate URLs with category fallback and one overall deadline; production logging defaults to info with LOG_LEVEL override and structured secret scrubbing; IGDB edition canonicalization uses the real version_parent relationship with request headroom and serialized parent lookup; browser authentication uses httpOnly cookies, a distinct random CSRF token, bearer compatibility, and a guarded legacy-token migration; affected clients use the shared base-path-aware apiFetch helper.

The self-signed SABnzbd retry was removed in d822e19d: TLS verification remains enabled even when the legacy allowSelfSignedCertificate field is true. Private CAs are supported through NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS or the OS/container trust store; the UI hides the ineffective toggle and explains this path.

The latest PR review had three unresolved threads. The StrictMode legacy-token migration and trusted-proxy cookie-secure findings are already handled in QuestarrNG. The logger finding was reproducible: Pino field formatting did not cover message text or child bindings. Commit 9924b48c adds redaction to the final serialized record and regression coverage for message, formatted message, and child-binding secrets.
acceptance: Unlisted API routes require authentication while only the intentional public-route allowlist remains public.
SABnzbd TLS connections always verify the certificate chain; the legacy bypass field cannot disable verification, and private CA trust uses NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS or the OS/container trust store.
xREL search has a finite request timeout and release nuke reasons are returned and shown.
Newznab and Torznab caps discovery falls back to game categories without multiplying the total request deadline.
Production logs default to info, LOG_LEVEL can override it, and structured fields, rendered messages, and child bindings are scrubbed before reaching log sinks.
IGDB version editions collapse only through explicit version_parent links, with request headroom for deduplication and parent requests subject to the shared limiter.
Cookie sessions are httpOnly, cookie-authenticated mutations require CSRF validation, bearer clients remain compatible, and a legacy localStorage token is migrated at most once per provider mount.
Add Game and downloads requests use the shared helper so base paths and auth headers are consistently applied.

items.title: Fix IGDB search 404 when QUESTARR_BASE_PATH is set

findings: The author closed this PR with the note that its changes were already part of #935. QuestarrNG AddGameModal and downloads page both use the shared apiFetch helper, which applies the configured base path and authorization consistently.
acceptance: Add Game IGDB search and downloads requests use the shared base-path-aware fetch helper; PR #935 carries the combined upstream change.

items.title: Fix SABnzbd manual Confirm Import source path resolution and retryability behavior

findings: PR #940 explicitly supersedes this first SABnzbd Confirm Import fix. The rebase retains idempotent completed-path resolution, uses the shared path-normalization helper, adds Windows backslash-path handling, and replaces risky trailing-separator regexes. QuestarrNG has the final behavior and regression coverage.
acceptance: SABnzbd manual confirm resolves folder and single-file history paths without duplicating the release segment, handles Windows-style incomplete paths, and remains retryable when confirmation fails.

items.title: Add safe recursive Scan Disk file discovery (rebase of #892)

findings: The rebased Scan Disk implementation provides a read-only recursive game-file scan with per-user ownership checks, files-only output, library-root containment checks, category inheritance, and normalization of packs to the persisted extra category. The fork also carries later scan budgets and rate limiting; PR #892 is already recorded as superseded by this rebase.
acceptance: Scanning an owned game's library returns only contained files with normalized categories; missing or escaping paths return an empty result, access is owner-scoped, and the recursive walk respects configured file/time limits and rate limiting.

items.title: Keep instances out of search engine indexes

findings: The application sends X-Robots-Tag noindex, nofollow on responses, serves a disallow-all robots.txt, and includes a noindex meta tag in the HTML. The security assessment correctly explains that these signals do not remove already-indexed pages or replace authentication. The follow-up security-header regression is verified separately in #941.
acceptance: All application responses carry the anti-indexing header, robots.txt disallows crawlers, the HTML has a noindex meta tag, and documentation describes the limits of crawler directives.

items.title: Fix SABnzbd manual Confirm Import path resolution + SonarCloud regex fixes

findings: This PR rebases and supersedes #937. QuestarrNG uses the shared buildRemoteImportPath and stripTrailingPathSeparators helpers instead of duplicate path logic or backtracking-prone separator regexes. SABnzbd history resolution handles completed folders, single-file storage paths, and Windows backslash-delimited incomplete paths.
acceptance: Manual-confirm paths avoid duplicate release suffixes, completed folder and single-file history paths resolve correctly, Windows separators are handled, and path normalization avoids the flagged super-linear regex behavior.

items.title: Fix /robots.txt bypassing security headers

findings: The robots.txt response route is registered in routes.ts after Helmet middleware, so it receives the application's security headers; the early X-Robots-Tag middleware remains in app.ts to cover earlier error responses. The single upstream inline review thread is resolved.
acceptance: robots.txt keeps the disallow-all response and receives configured Helmet security headers, including X-Content-Type-Options nosniff; early responses still receive the X-Robots-Tag header.

items.title: Add --ignore-scripts to npm ci in CI workflow and Dockerfile

findings: Dockerfile and CI npm ci installs use --ignore-scripts consistently, avoiding lifecycle scripts during dependency installation. The upstream checks were green and had no actionable review feedback.
acceptance: All npm ci invocations in the Docker build and CI workflow pass --ignore-scripts.

items.title: Add root folder scanning to discover existing games on disk

findings: Root-folder discovery, validation, storage, deletion, scanning, UI, and documentation are present. The reviewed fixes are reflected: unmatched folders are validated against the server-queued absolute path, changed paths are probed before persistence, all configured roots are scanned, existing libraryPath values are preserved, deletion is separately opt-in, and failures produce a user-visible error.
Root folders use shared instance-admin configuration like indexers and downloaders, consistent with the documented self-hosted multi-user model; they are not user-owned rows.
acceptance: Users can discover and queue root folders, review matches, scan configured roots, and remove entries while file deletion remains opt-in.
Server-side validation and path probes protect persisted root configuration from client-controlled or invalid paths.

items.title: Bound the recursive Scan Disk endpoint (file count, size, depth, duration, rate limit)

findings: The endpoint already met the explicit acceptance for a 5,000-file cap, 5-second wall-clock budget, { files, truncated } response, per-user 10-requests-per-minute limiter, and count/time/rate tests. The traversal was strengthened to stream directory entries instead of materializing a whole directory and now also caps encoded response size at 8 MiB and nesting depth at 128.

The Files tab now retains the response truncation flag and announces when the displayed list is partial, so users do not mistake a bounded scan for a complete inventory. Upstream PR #955 implements the original count/time/rate acceptance.
acceptance: Recursive scans stop at 5,000 files, 8 MiB encoded response, depth 128, or 5 seconds; any cap returns truncated: true.
The endpoint is limited to 10 requests per minute per authenticated user and its count, time, size, depth, and rate limits have regression coverage.
The Files tab explains partial results accessibly while still displaying returned files.

items.title: Move Discord webhook config from Settings to Stats page

items.title: Make downloader self-signed-certificate TLS bypass opt-in

findings: The request makes a self-signed-certificate bypass opt-in. QuestarrNG has removed the request-level TLS-verification bypass entirely; certificate validation stays enabled even when the legacy allowSelfSignedCertificate database field is true.

The old checkbox is hidden and replaced with guidance to trust a private CA through NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS or the operating system/container trust store. This is stricter than opt-in bypass and avoids exposing SABnzbd API keys or archive passwords to an untrusted certificate.
acceptance: SABnzbd HTTPS always validates the peer certificate; stale settings cannot disable validation.
Operators can trust private/local certificate authorities through the supported CA trust store configuration.

items.title: xREL: add request timeout to searchReleases; capture and surface nuke reason

The upstream SonarCloud Code Analysis quality gate failed because new-code duplication measured 18.4% against a 3% maximum. The remaining upstream CI, security, build, and test checks succeeded; local focused validation passes the fork implementation tests.
acceptance: A stalled xREL search fails within the bounded request timeout.
Nuke reason and flag data reach the UI as visible text and badge rather than hover-only information.

items.title: Reorganize Settings page tabs by domain

acceptance: Settings tabs group controls by domain and preserve existing save behavior.
Blacklist entries remain scoped to their game and can be removed with an accessible name.
IGDB per-user rate limits are restricted to integer values 1 through 4 and successful saves give clear feedback.

items.title: IGDB: canonicalize/dedupe game editions in search results

findings: IGDB edition results are canonicalized through version_parent and deduplicated before local filters run. Search requests retain headroom for local filtering and fall back to the original results if canonicalization would otherwise make the result set empty.
acceptance: Edition searches return one canonical base-game result, preserve platform/year filtering, and do not lose all results after local filtering.

items.title: Harden Newznab/Torznab caps (category) discovery

findings: Bounded caps discovery and category fallback are already present and were covered by Batch 82. This batch exposes whether categories were discovered or supplied as fallback through X-Questarr-Category-Source and shows an accessible localized notice so users can confirm provider support before selecting fallback suggestions.
acceptance: Newznab/Torznab discovery retains its overall deadline and fallback behavior.
The fallback response identifies its provenance and the indexer editor announces the localized provider-confirmation guidance.

items.title: Fix production log level hardcoded to debug; add secret redaction

findings: Production logging defaults to info, supports LOG_LEVEL, and scrubs serialized records after message formatting, including structured fields and child bindings.
acceptance: Production logging uses the configured level and secrets are removed from the complete emitted record.

items.title: Fix unauthenticated GET /api/config; add default-deny API auth boundary

findings: API routes use a default-deny authentication boundary with an explicit public-route allowlist; unauthenticated GET /api/config does not expose protected configuration.
acceptance: Unauthenticated config requests are denied and protected routes remain behind the default-deny boundary.

items.title: Migrate auth to httpOnly cookies + CSRF, with bearer-token fallback

Legacy localStorage tokens are now removed from persistent storage but tried only after cookie authentication returns 401 or 403, preventing a stale bearer token from overriding a valid cookie session. The updated client tests and browser behavior still need private-JIT validation.
acceptance: Cookie auth is attempted first on /api/auth/me.
A legacy token is used only as a one-time fallback candidate after an unauthorized cookie response and remains in memory only after successful validation.
Login/logout clear legacy bearer state and UI session changes pass browser verification.

items.title: Bound the recursive Scan Disk endpoint (file count, time budget, rate limit)

items.title: Add SABnzbd archive password support for G4U-style releases

Downloader password transmission requires HTTPS and credential-bearing redirects remain same-origin.
Passwords are masked in API responses, excluded from validation diagnostics, and limited to 200 characters.

The desktop result table renders a priority value for each row.

findings: Ported the category fallback and five regression cases from upstream commit 58d984d2cda90f1b04fffb5deffb15527dbeeec5 (author Vincent A). The focused SABnzbd regression suites pass, and all three downloader suites pass (67 tests).

Authenticated Questarr API integration against SABnzbd 5.1.3 verified category save/reload and Test Connection. A download without a request category entered the saved category; an explicit request category overrode it; the adapter's empty-configuration fallback is games. SABnzbd mapped an unregistered category to * (Default), documented as an operator setup requirement. The disposable queue was cleared and no Usenet server was configured.

A live source refresh captured the reporter's October 13 follow-up: after upgrading from 1.5.0 RC1 to the latest release, the category behavior works as intended. This confirms the existing verified resolution.
acceptance: Explicit request category overrides downloader category.
Missing or empty request category uses downloader category.
Absent/empty configured category falls back to games.
Saved category survives the actual Questarr API round trip and is honored by a real SABnzbd instance.
The configured category exists in SABnzbd; unregistered categories are documented as appearing under its default category.
evidence: Focused downloader test suites: 67 passed; full suite at the current source baseline: 4,009 passed, 7 skipped
